title: Interior recovery of the two Airy coefficients
source_hypothesis: Actual classical glancing phase and finite complex matrix amplitudes, invertible boundary g0 and zero boundary h; fixed sufficiently small strictly interior slab; nested compact input/output base and conic supports. Constants depend on that fixed slab. The obstruction uses exact affine normalized Airy solutions.
reviewed_arguments: The actual classical phase and complex matrix amplitudes are retained. Observation and input cutoffs have nested compact margins; the slab is fixed strictly inside the collar and constants are not claimed uniform as it approaches the boundary.
Exact Airy identities give the two branch coefficients f plus or minus i k. Only the scalar Airy mode is conjugated; the complex matrix amplitudes remain unchanged.

Differentiated negative-ray expansions become ordinary symbols on the fixed interior slab. The mixed graph matrix stays invertible and the leading branch amplitude is elliptic of order minus one sixth.

The normalized output covector images, including different input frequencies, are separated on compact reduced patches. Actual ordinary observation operators remove the opposite branch with a fully smoothing kernel.
Full Sobolev conjugation followed by uniform fixed-q graph estimates proves all-real mapping. Kernel-adjoint duality gives the exact adjoint shift without restricting rough fields to a slice.

The normal operator is the integral of fixed-q graph products. All symbol and remainder bounds are uniform in the compact normal variable. Its matrix Gram principal symbol is positive elliptic of order minus one third.

A supported ordered matrix parametrix produces a single fixed coefficient extraction operator bounded from H^r to H^(r-1/6). Exact composition gives both localized coefficients plus full smooth remainders.

The reverse estimate retains arbitrary finite coarse norms and explicit observation-error norms. Distributional regularity follows from the identity without assuming the coefficient regularity in advance.

Both physical signs identify the opposite branch coefficient with the stable decaying coefficient alpha. The other extraction retains the order B0 Z_epsilon; no inverse exponential multiplier or unsupported commutation is used.
Bounded extraction of an arbitrary energy field is distinguished from reconstructing every PDE solution. Complete representation and the remaining boundary estimate are not claimed.

An exact affine normalized Airy packet has order-one stable boundary norm and exponentially small norms of every order on the fixed interior slab. The packet proves failure of an interior-only boundary-weight estimate even with any fixed negative Sobolev remainder.

Three solved exercises cover both coefficient signs, exact affine canonical coordinates and normal symbols, and quantitative smooth-error dependence. Twenty-two exact symbolic checks accompany the analytic proofs.
All thirteen final lesson captures were inspected, including the complete original figure and two mobile samples. All 253 formulas and 22 displays parse and horizontal extents remain accessible.

The combined boundary-weighted reverse estimate, enhanced trace recovery, controlled residual removal and general energy representation remain active, together with every other full AN-04 obligation. The 92 inherited human proofs remain external.
